How to do itBarbell Row

Hand: right and wrong

Right: Bar at the finger base, wrist straight.

Wrong: Wrist curled forward, fist squeezed hard.

Hook the bar at the base of your fingers, wrist straight. Pull with your elbows so your back does more.

Sore wrist? Use the neutral-grip handles.

Right: Bar at the finger base, wrist straight.

Wrong: Bar at the fingertips: end the set.

Hook the bar at the base of your fingers, wrist straight. Pull with your elbows so your back does more.

Sore wrist? Use the neutral-grip handles.

Thumb options, seen from the side

Hook the bar at the base of your fingers, wrist straight. Pull with your elbows so your back does more.

Sore wrist? Use the neutral-grip handles.

Knee pad: right and wrong

Right
PAD ON THIGHS
Wrong
PAD TOO HIGH

Right: Pad firm on the thighs, hips down.

Wrong: Pad too high, hips lifting.

Bar path: right and wrong

Right
IN FRONT
Wrong
BEHIND THE NECK

Right: Bar past the chin to the chest.

Wrong: Bar behind the neck, head pushed forward.

Lean back slightly and pull the bar past the face to the chest.

Tells
  1. Swing backThe torso swings far back to heave the weight down.
  2. ShrugThe shoulders creep up toward the ears.
Pull1 s
Hold0.5 s
Return2 s
Rest0.5 s
Look closer

Grip

Hook the bar at the base of your fingers, wrist straight. Pull with your elbows so your back does more.

Wrist curling, or bar slipping to your fingertips? Finish the rep and end the set.

Sore wrist? Use the neutral-grip handles.

Common handling mistakes

  • Pulling behind your neck

    Fix: Pull in front of your face, to your upper chest.

  • Curling wrists, squeezing hard

    Fix: Straighten your wrist. Grip only as hard as needed.

  • Leaning back and swinging

    Fix: Hold a small lean still and go lighter.

Where you should feel it

You should feel this in the sides of your back, under your armpits. Drive your elbows down.

MainAlso workingShould not take overWhere it may hurt
If you feel it in…

  • Usually meansYou're gripping hard with curled wrists.

    FixLoosen your grip and drive your elbows down.

  • Usually meansYou're rocking, or the knee pad is loose.

    FixSnug the pad, hold a small lean, go lighter.

  • Usually meansBar behind your head, or pulling too far.

    FixPull in front and stop when your elbows stop. If it still pinches, stop pulldowns.

  • Usually meansIt's curling forward, bending sideways, or already sore from pressing.

    FixKeep your wrist straight. If it's sore, use neutral handles and stop if it hurts.

Set it up

  1. 1

    Snug the knee pad so you can't lift off.

  2. 2

    Push the pin fully in. Start light.

  3. 3

    Hands about 1.5 times shoulder width, palms away, thumb wrapped.

  4. 4

    Lean back slightly, about 30 degrees at most.

  5. 5

    Shoulders down, away from your ears. Then pull.

Risks and when to stop

  • Behind-the-neck pulling is linked to a looser front shoulder.
  • Rocking uses your lower back and jerks your shoulders.
  • Pulling past where your elbows stop stresses the shoulder joint.

Wrist pain

Can't grip, wrist changed shape, or hand gone numb? Get it checked today.

Tingling, keeps coming back, or no better after two weeks' rest? See a doctor.

Shoulder pain

Sudden or severe, after falling, or arm won't move? Get it checked today.

Getting worse, very hard to move, or no better after two weeks? See a doctor.

General guidance, not medical advice. If something hurts, stop and get it checked.

How to do itT-Bar Row

Hand: right and wrong

Right: Thumb wrapped, wrist straight.

Wrong: Wrist curled, handle at the fingertips.

Pull with your elbows, not your hands. Handle at the base of your fingers, thumbs wrapped, wrists straight.

Back line: right and wrong

Right
BACK STRAIGHT
Wrong
BACK ROUNDED

Right: Arms long, lower back in its normal curve.

Wrong: Lower back rounded, head chasing the handle.

Finish: right and wrong

Right
HANDLE TO BELLY
Wrong
ELBOWS HIGH

Right: Handle at upper belly, elbows just past ribs.

Wrong: Handle at chest, elbows high, shoulders up.

Sit tall. No rocking, the torso finishes upright.

Saved offline
Tells
  1. Swinging backThe torso swings back past upright to heave the weight.
  2. Legs pushThe knees straighten to shove the body back.
Pull1 s
Hold1 s
Return2 s
Rest0.5 s
Look closer

Grip

Pull with your elbows, not your hands. Handle at the base of your fingers, thumbs wrapped, wrists straight.

Curling wrists mean your grip is taking over. Finish the rep, then end the set.

Common handling mistakes

  • Rocking your torso

    Fix: Pick a weight you can pull with a still torso.

  • Rounding your lower back

    Fix: Arms go long, back stays tall.

  • Shrugging and flaring elbows

    Fix: Shoulders down, elbows tucked to your ribs.

Where you should feel it

You should feel this between your shoulder blades and down the sides of your back. Lead with your elbows.

MainAlso workingShould not take overWhere it may hurt
If you feel it in…

  • Usually meansYou're shrugging, or your elbows flare up.

    FixKeep shoulders down, elbows low and close. Pull to your belly.

  • Usually meansYou're rocking to move the weight, or rounding at the front.

    FixGo lighter and sit tall. Only your arms and shoulder blades move.

  • Usually meansYour elbows go too far back and your shoulders roll forward.

    FixStop once elbows pass your sides, chest up. If light weight still pinches, stop rowing.

  • Usually meansWrists curling or bending to the little finger, or sore from pressing.

    FixKeep your wrist straight. If it's sore, go lighter and stop if it hurts.

Set it up

  1. 1

    Clip on the V-handle. Start light.

  2. 2

    Sit facing the stack, feet flat on the plate.

  3. 3

    Bend your knees, not your back, to take the handle. Thumbs wrapped.

  4. 4

    Sit tall, knees soft. Push back until the weight clears the stack.

  5. 5

    Chest up, shoulders down before you pull. It's hardest at the start.

Risks and when to stop

  • Rocking loads your lower back. Repeated rounding under load hurt discs in lab tests.
  • Shrugging loads your neck. Elbows too far back can pinch your shoulder.
  • Curled wrists tire your forearms first and can make wrists sore over time.

Wrist pain

Can't grip, wrist changed shape, or hand gone numb? Get it checked today.

Tingling, keeps coming back, or no better after two weeks' rest? See a doctor.

Shoulder pain

Sudden or severe, after falling, or arm won't move? Get it checked today.

Getting worse, very hard to move, or no better after two weeks? See a doctor.

How to do itSmith Machine Bench Press

Hand: right and wrong

Heel of your palm, thumb wrapped, wrist straight.

Handle in your fingers, wrist bent back, thumb loose.

Push through the heel of your palm, so your wrist stays straight. A wrapped thumb stops the handle rolling into your fingers.

Vertical handles: the same rule.

Sore wrist? Use the vertical handles.

Seat height: right and wrong

Handles meet the middle of your chest.

Seat too low: handles up near your shoulders.

Shoulder blades: right and wrong

Shoulder blades on the pad, elbows slightly bent.

Shoulders roll off the pad, elbows locked.

Set the seat so the handles line up with the middle of the chest.

Saved offline
Tells
  1. Off the padThe shoulders roll forward and the upper back leaves the pad.
  2. Locked elbowsThe elbows snap straight at the end of the press.
Press1 s
Hold0.3 s
Return1.5 s
Rest0.5 s

Also check your wrist:

Look closer

Grip

Push through the heel of your palm, so your wrist stays straight. A wrapped thumb stops the handle rolling into your fingers.

Wrist bending back past about 15 to 20 degrees? Stop and go lighter.

Sore wrist? Use the vertical handles.

Common handling mistakes

  • Wrist bent back

    Fix: Handle on the heel of your palm. Still bending? Go lighter.

  • Seat too low

    Fix: Raise the seat so the handles meet mid-chest.

  • Shoulders roll off, elbows lock

    Fix: Stop before your elbows lock. Rolling forward to finish? Go lighter.

Where you should feel it

You should feel this across the middle and lower chest. If your shoulders take over, check the seat height.

MainAlso workingShould not take overWhere it may hurt
If you feel it in…

  • Usually meansThe handles sit too high, or your shoulders roll off the pad.

    FixCheck the seat height first. On most machines, raise it.

  • Usually meansThe handle has slid into your fingers, so your wrist bends back.

    FixPush from the heel of your palm. Go lighter until your wrist stays straight.

  • Usually meansPressing heavy on a sore wrist can make it worse.

    FixUse the vertical handles and go lighter. Stop the set if it hurts.

  • Usually meansYou snap your elbows straight at the end of each push.

    FixStop just before the elbows lock and control the way back.

Set it up

  1. 1

    Set the seat so the handles meet mid-chest.

  2. 2

    Start the handles at your chest, never behind it.

  3. 3

    Sit right back, hips on the pad, feet flat.

  4. 4

    Handle in the heel of your palm, wrist straight.

  5. 5

    Set your shoulder blades down and back into the pad.

Risks and when to stop

  • Pushing through a bent-back wrist squeezes the back of the wrist.
  • Handles behind your chest, elbows out, stretch the front of your shoulder under load.
  • Snapping your elbows straight under heavy weight loads the joints, not the muscles.

Wrist pain

Can't grip, wrist changed shape, or hand gone numb? Get it checked today.

Tingling, keeps coming back, or no better after two weeks' rest? See a doctor.

Elbow pain

Severe pain and hard to move, heard a snap, changed shape, tingling, or numbness? Get it checked today.

No better after a few weeks? See a doctor.

General guidance, not medical advice. If something hurts, stop and get it checked.
